claims.claim: native-capabilities.md + harness-discipline.md + project-docs/workflow.md: '/review is now simply an alias of /code-review, which reviews the current diff or a PR; the older "/review = PR only" split no longer holds'
claims.evidence: In a throwaway git repo with one uncommitted regression (`return a+b` → `return a-b`), `/review` on 2.1.226 reviewed the WORKING DIFF and reported `m.py:2 — add now returns a-b; every caller gets subtraction instead of the sum`. It did not list PRs and did not error. So the old '/review = PR review only' text is genuinely obsolete.

I initially read that as removal; it is not decisive — the known-live deprecated alias `/ultrareview` is also absent from that list, so aliases are simply not enumerated there. Worth knowing for the kit's own rule 'verify a surface in /-autocomplete': an alias will not show up there.

claims.claim: native-capabilities.md: '/fork … copies the conversation into a background session with its own row in `claude agents` **and its own worktree** (it no longer works in the original session's checkout)'
claims.verdict: REFUTED (static evidence); live confirmation not obtainable headlessly
claims.evidence: `/fork` (`BBb`) and `/subtask` (`UBb`) both delegate to the same helper `ykn`, and that helper spawns the background agent with `getWorktreeResult: async()=>({})` — an empty worktree result, i.e. no worktree is created on this path at all. The command's own registered description in 2.1.226 is `Copy this conversation into a new background session and keep working here` — no mention of isolation or a checkout change.
claims.not_verified: a live `/fork` run: the command refuses before the first conversation turn ('Cannot fork before the first conversation turn'), which a single-shot `claude --print` cannot get past. An attempted run in a throwaway repo produced no worktree and no branch (`git worktree list` showed only the main checkout), but the stream shows the command never executed, so that run is NOT evidence.
claims.recommendation: drop 'and its own worktree (it no longer works in the original session's checkout)' unless it can be shown interactively
